title: Relational synchronisation and prior-analogy combination audit
question: Can proximity to other beings, combined with the earlier pi, Fibonacci, entropy, halving, kappa-flow, phase-defect and negative-index analogies, affect RH?

verdict.conclusion: Proximity, Fibonacci cohorts and the squared positive splice kernel produce a valid attractive consensus graph.  Circular phase locking, a common pi register and reflection entropy leave horizontal zero support unchanged.  Horizontal consensus, golden contraction, halving and barycentric projection can move support, but then they change the off-line quartet polynomial.  Across all 127 non-empty combinations, every same-xi combination is support-inert and every support-changing combination lacks same-xi/principal-prime invariance.  The detectors remain detectors; no combination proves RH.

counterexample.label: perfect circular-phase lock with off-line support

sectorSeparation.meaning: q=0 and m=0 give perfect circular synchrony and maximal branch balance while eta=1/4 retains a positive RH defect and two negative squares

relationalHorizontalConsensus.goldenAlignment: at t=log(phi)/(2J), eta_+-eta_- is divided by phi
relationalHorizontalConsensus.halvingAlignment: at t=log(2)/(2J), eta_+-eta_- is divided by 2

fibonacciSpliceProximityGraph.edgeLaw: J_ab=exp(-distance)*sqrt(F_a F_b)/21*(K(u_a,u_b)/54)^2, with direct reflected-pair edges F_n/21
fibonacciSpliceProximityGraph.whySquared: the Gram kernel is PSD but can be pointwise negative; squaring makes each synchronising edge nonnegative

combinationCensus.reason: the audited maps act independently on q, m, eta or the schedule; introducing an eta-phase cross-law simply creates another support-changing flow whose arithmetic invariance must still be proved
